title: the siege
hook: a king who leaps into a fight, a messenger who won't be held, and the gates of Lanka
carry: peace offered, even at the gates

segments.voice: Yesterday: the siege began with two spies caught and set free. Rama hid nothing, and they went home urging peace. Nothing to hide.

Rama climbs Mount Suvela with his leaders to look at Lanka. And there, on a high tower across the way, stands Ravana himself, in royal clothes, among his attendants. Sugriva can't stand it. Without a word to anyone he leaps across, lands on the tower, knocks off Ravana's crown, and the two kings wrestle. Then Sugriva jumps back, pleased with himself. Rama is not pleased. A king doesn't do that, he says. If something had happened to you, what would I have done?
screen: `RAVANA ON HIS TOWER.` → `SUGRIVA LEAPS ACROSS.` → `A KING DOESN'T DO THAT.`

segments.voice: Then Rama does things in order. Lanka has four great gates, and he assigns a leader to each: Nila to the east, Angada to the south, Hanuman to the west, and Rama himself, with Lakshmana, to the north, where Ravana is. The city is surrounded. And still, before the first blow, Rama sends a messenger: Angada, Vali's son. Angada leaps to Ravana's palace and speaks plainly: return Sita, ask pardon, and you'll live. If not, this is the end of your line, and Vibhishana will rule Lanka. Ravana orders him seized. Four rakshasas grab him by the arms. Angada lets them. Then he springs onto the palace roof with all four still hanging on, and they drop off and fall to the ground. He stamps on the roof's peak, breaks it, and leaps back to Rama. You may know a different scene here: Angada planting his foot in Ravana's court, and no one able to lift it. That comes from later tellings, especially Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas. In Valmiki it's the broken rooftop. Either way, Rama made a final offer of peace, in person, with the city already surrounded. Only after Angada returns does the battle begin. The monkeys swarm the walls with trees and rocks, the rakshasas pour out of the gates, and the siege of Lanka becomes a war.
screen: `FOUR GATES, FOUR LEADERS.` · `ANGADA CARRIES THE LAST OFFER.` · `FOUR RAKSHASAS AND A ROOFTOP.` · `THE FOOT IN COURT CAME LATER.` · then, large: `PEACE OFFERED, EVEN AT THE GATES.`

segments.voice: Think of a conflict you're in, at home or at work, and notice whether part of you is ready to leap at someone's tower like Sugriva. Breathe slowly, and hold one quiet question without answering it yet: have I made a plain offer of peace?
The siege. Lanka's four gates surrounded, and one last offer of peace carried by Angada, before the first battle begins.
Your line: peace offered, even at the gates. The war's first night is coming. That's day six hundred forty.

howItsDone: In North Indian Ramlila performances, Angada's embassy to Ravana's court is a well-known scene, often played in the Ramcharitmanas version with Angada's unmovable foot.

original.note: Sanskrit Aṅgada: Vali's son; the word also names an armlet, an ornament worn on the upper arm.

trapdoor: what you thought: Rama attacked as soon as he reached Lanka.
what it means: he surrounded the city, then sent Angada with one more offer of peace.
what a scholar hears: the famous immovable foot of Angada belongs to later tellings, especially Tulsidas; Valmiki has the broken rooftop.

chat.says: If Rama already had Lanka surrounded, why bother sending Angada to talk?
options: To give Ravana one last chance: return Sita, ask pardon, and live.
To spy on the palace and count Ravana's soldiers before the attack.
To demand that Ravana hand Lanka's throne over to Angada himself.
chat.meaning: Even with the city surrounded, Rama sends a plain, final offer of peace. Only after Angada returns does the battle begin.

Suvela.meaning: the mountain where Rama's leaders look out over Lanka

Angada.meaning: Vali's son, a young monkey prince in Rama's army

Sugriva.meaning: king of the monkeys, Rama's ally

Tulsidas.meaning: the poet who wrote the Ramcharitmanas

Ramcharitmanas.meaning: Tulsidas's Hindi retelling of Rama's story

recall: a mountain rising to offer Hanuman rest
a headless trunk, all arms and belly
